title: Event ordering and parallel processing
prompt: An e-commerce site needs to process updates for the same order in sequence while processing different orders concurrently. Workers may stop temporarily. Which architecture is best?

choices.text: Use SQS FIFO and set the order ID as the MessageGroupId
choices.explanation: Messages within the same group are ordered, while different groups can be processed concurrently.

choices.text: Use SQS FIFO and set the same MessageGroupId for every order
choices.explanation: This preserves order, but a single group limits concurrent processing.

choices.text: Deliver from an SNS standard topic to an SQS standard queue without managing order
choices.explanation: This provides a durable buffer but does not provide strict ordering per order.

choices.text: Use an SQS standard queue and increase the number of workers
choices.explanation: A standard queue does not guarantee strict message ordering.

learning.reason: Messages within the same group are ordered, while different groups can be processed concurrently.
learning.concept: The granularity of the group key lets you control both ordering guarantees and concurrency.

title: Restricting delivery of static assets
prompt: A CloudFront distribution delivers subscriber-only files stored in S3. Users may download them only after their subscription has been verified in the application, and direct access to S3 must be blocked. Which two settings should be configured?

choices.text: Use the public URL of the S3 static website as the origin
choices.explanation: This conflicts with blocking direct access to S3.

choices.text: Issue CloudFront signed URLs after verifying the subscription
choices.explanation: This controls viewer access by resource and expiration time.

choices.text: Set only a long cache TTL in CloudFront
Block public access to S3 and configure a bucket policy that allows only CloudFront OAC
choices.explanation: This allows CloudFront to access S3 while preventing direct public access.

choices.text: Only create an S3 access point for the origin
choices.explanation: This does not enforce subscription verification for users.

learning.reason: Allow access from CloudFront to S3 while preventing direct public access. Control viewer access by resource and expiration time.
learning.concept: Configure viewer authorization separately from authentication between CloudFront and the origin.

title: Preventing frequent connections from overwhelming the database
prompt: When Lambda concurrency rises sharply, the RDS connection limit is reached even though the DB has spare CPU capacity. The existing RDS engine must be retained, and connections should be reused through a managed mechanism.

choices.text: Point Lambda to RDS Proxy and pool connections
choices.explanation: It reuses many short-lived connections through a pool and can reduce the number of connections the DB must maintain concurrently.

choices.text: Only add a read replica to the same DB
choices.explanation: This does not add a pool for the write connection target.
This does not reuse connections to the DB.

choices.text: Shorten the DB backup retention period
choices.explanation: Backup settings do not manage runtime connections.

learning.reason: It reuses many short-lived connections through a pool and can reduce the number of connections the DB must maintain concurrently.
learning.concept: Consider connection limits separately from processing capacity. Frequent session pinning reduces the benefit of pooling.

title: Delivering static files from each release immediately
prompt: A web application behind CloudFront must reference new JavaScript from its HTML immediately after a release. Users who received old HTML must also continue to have a working application, and a full cache invalidation on every release should be avoided.

choices.text: Overwrite files using the same names and set long TTLs for the HTML and JavaScript
choices.explanation: The old JavaScript may remain cached, mismatching the new HTML.

choices.text: Delete the old files immediately before each new release
choices.explanation: This breaks references from old HTML.
This may improve consistency, but it loses cache reuse through versioned names, and old HTML reads the new asset at the same URL.

choices.text: Include a content hash in each static filename, retain old and new assets in parallel, and configure HTML to be revalidated
choices.explanation: The referenced URL differs by version, and old pages can still retrieve the old files.

learning.reason: The referenced URL differs by version, and old pages can still retrieve the old files.
learning.concept: Use separate cache policies for HTML and static assets, and retain old files for as long as old HTML or clients may still exist.
